I farm only 4.1 mu, so every bag of input matters, but I still will not hold back too much on fertilizer because if cotton grows weak, I cannot get that yield back later. I usually start from what I did before and then adjust a little. On my land in Quzhou, with well irrigation, I will plant cotton in spring and use an improved variety, because the newer kinds usually set bolls more evenly and do better if the weather turns against me. I will plough the field first, because cotton likes a deeper, cleaner seedbed than just scratching the top. For fertilizer, I will aim around 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu for the year. I will put most of the phosphorus and part of the nitrogen and potassium in as base fertilizer, then topdress the rest in stages around squaring and boll setting. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the plants go pale and short. Since I have well water, I will irrigate about 4 times if rainfall is not enough: once after establishment if the soil is dry, once at squaring, once at flowering, and once at boll filling. For pests, I will watch the field closely and spray about 5 times in the season, depending on aphids, bollworm, and later sucking pests. If the year is smooth, I may save one spray, but I will budget for 5. On 4.1 mu, I mostly do the work myself, so I will keep the plan simple and steady, not fancy. If weather is normal and pests are controlled, I will look for about 320 kg per mu.
